title: Claude Opus 5.5 built this character in Blender from a concept sheet, all in Python. I turned the workflow into an open-source skill
author: MajidManzarpour
selftext:
Claude Opus 5.5 built this character in Blender from one concept sheet, entirely by writing Blender Python in Claude Code. No sculpting, no generators, and I didn't model anything by hand. I prompted, reviewed and gave feedback.  
  
To be upfront, it wasn't one prompt. It took iterating: the face was rebuilt once, and the hands, neck and hair each took a few passes. I also generated extra 2D reference angles where the sheet was too small to read (face/neck/hands). The more detailed 2D references you have, the better outcome you should see. Some references in thread: [https://x.com/majidmanzarpour/status/2102920224718873027](https://x.com/majidmanzarpour/status/2102920224718873027)  
  
I packaged the workflow as my first Blender skill for game dev, **blender-image-to-3d**. It works in phases, and at each one it renders the model beside your references and measures the difference before moving on.

Open source (MIT), for Claude Code:

    npx skills add majidmanzarpour/blender-game-skills --skill blender-image-to-3d

[https://github.com/majidmanzarpour/blender-game-skills](https://github.com/majidmanzarpour/blender-game-skills)
